claims.text: Transitioning HfNbTaTiZr from a random solid solution to HfTi- or TiZr-like B2 ordering reduces local lattice distortion.
Reduced lattice distortion shifts the high-frequency phonon DOS to higher frequencies.
B2-like ordering reduces phonon scattering rates in HfNbTaTiZr.
The reduced scattering produces a net increase in lattice thermal conductivity despite the presence of SRO clusters.
The initial HfNbTaTiZr state contains significant HfTi and TiZr SRO clusters but lacks long-range B2-like order.
Thermal annealing or related processing can convert the SRO clusters into long-range ordered B2-like binary phases.
The induced ordered domains form percolating pathways through the alloy.
The conductivity-increase mechanism requires retention of the BCC structure and attainment of an SRO-cluster percolation threshold.
Atomic displacement amplitudes are lower inside ordered B2 domains than in random SRO regions.
Long-range chemical ordering minimizes local chemical disorder and associated lattice strain.
Reduced local disorder and strain suppress scattering of high-frequency phonons and increase their mean free paths.
The reduction in disorder scattering outweighs scattering introduced by the SRO clusters and ordered-domain boundaries.
Compared with the random state, the ordered state will exhibit higher lattice thermal conductivity, higher-energy high-frequency DOS peaks, and a lower root-mean-square atomic displacement.
High chemical disorder and lattice distortion in the random solid solution strongly scatter phonons and produce low thermal conductivity.
A conductivity increase occurs only when the ordered B2 domains form a percolating network.
If the ordered phase remains isolated, conductivity will decrease.
Ordering can induce brittle secondary phases such as the Laves phases reported in Al-Cr-Fe-Mn-Ti systems, causing decreased conductivity or mechanical failure.
Complex oxides can be detrimental in a B2-containing refractory alloy, but they bound the stability of the proposed HfNbTaTiZr B2 phase through decomposition.
The base Ta0.5Nb0.5HfZrTi alloy cited in the evidence contained 0.377 at.% oxygen from fabrication.
Oxygen content could interfere with the proposed B2-ordering and conductivity mechanism.

contradictions.description: The starting state is called a random solid solution while also being described as containing significant chemically specific HfTi and TiZr SRO clusters. Significant SRO implies non-random local chemical correlations, so the intended distinction between fully random, SRO-containing, and long-range-ordered states is not defined consistently.
